name: Home screen widgets
plain: Small live panels on the home screen that the person adds themselves; refresh rates are capped on both systems.
meaning: Widgets keep an app visible without opening it. Android refreshes on a timer (30 min minimum) or by push; iOS gives each widget a daily budget of about 40 to 70 refreshes.

android.prompt_ui: User long presses home screen and adds the widget
android.note: updatePeriodMillis minimum 30 min; widget bitmaps are size capped on Android 17; Android 12 added reconfigure and responsive layouts

ios.note: Budget roughly 40 to 70 timeline reloads per day per widget, shorter when the widget is visible; push reloads via WidgetPushHandler (iOS 26) are budgeted too

limits.headline: Can show live info on your home screen, but only refresh a limited number of times
limits.user_action: You add the widget yourself from the widget gallery or by long pressing the home screen
can: Show a small panel with the latest data on your home screen
Refresh every 30 minutes at best on Android, or on a push signal
Change when you tap or reconfigure it
cannot: Refresh more than about 40 to 70 times a day on iPhone
Run live at the second level; updates are spaced out
Use large images on Android 17 beyond the size cap
limits.reach_label: Small, spaced out, after you add it
limits.differs: Android refreshes on a timer of 30 minutes or more, or by push. iPhone gives a daily refresh budget.

story.what_it_is: Small live panels you put on the home screen, such as weather, steps or a timer.

marketing.name: Widgets
marketing.pitch: Get information you care about at a glance, right on the Home Screen and Lock Screen.

marketing.name: App widgets
marketing.pitch: Add small views of an app's key info and actions to the Android home screen.

story.for_you: You pick a widget and put it where you want. You see the weather, score or timer without opening the app, and a tap jumps into it.
story.for_makers: A widget keeps an app on the screen all day, which brings people back. Both systems cap how often a widget can refresh, so makers choose smart moments or push updates to save battery.

use_cases.example: A sports app widget shows the live score of tonight's game, and the number changes while you watch.
A step and ring widget keeps your daily goal in view and nudges you to finish.
A game widget shows when your farm crops are ready or when the next energy refill arrives.
A live widget shows your ride's arrival time on the lock screen as the car approaches.
A food delivery widget counts down minutes until the courier arrives.
Brands gain a spot on the home screen, which counts as free daily attention for a store or bank.
A task widget lets you tick off a to do item without opening the app.

risks: Battery use if refreshed too often
story.android_note: Android refreshes on a timer (30 minutes minimum) or by push.
story.ios_note: iOS gives each widget a daily budget of roughly 40 to 70 refreshes.

technical_bounds: Only the user can place a widget
Refresh budget is dynamic on iOS

history.change: WidgetKit and home screen widgets introduced
